city.caveat: This is the official city record as kept, without adjustments. It joins several observing sites over the years, and a move, a new instrument or the city growing around a station can shift readings (city growth mostly warms nights); NOAA's adjusted climate datasets correct for these. Treat any single number as approximate.

text.lede: Yesterday's high of 50°F was the 25th coolest November 13 high (tied) of 148 since 1879, the coolest since 2022.
text.p_yest: The high of 50°F was the 25th coolest November 13 high (tied) of 148 since 1879, the coolest since 2022. The normal high for the date is 62°F, and the record is 78°F (1931, 1938, 1964, 1989). The low of 40°F was typical for November 13.
text.t_rec: Record highs keep coming. Record lows have nearly stopped.
text.p_rec: If Chattanooga's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Chattanooga has set 12 standing record lows, far fewer than the 66 that chance alone would give, and 124 record highs, far more than the 66 that chance alone would give. The 2010s hold the most record highs of any decade (59). Chattanooga's all-time high is 107°F, on June 30, 2012.
text.t_chg: Chattanooga's nights have warmed since 1986. Its days have warmed.
text.p_chg: Across 147 complete years: Chattanooga's average low shows no clear change: −0.03°F per decade, a range (−0.10 to +0.04) that includes zero. Chattanooga's average high has risen +0.21°F per decade (95% range +0.15 to +0.26), about +3.0°F since 1879. The last 40 years tell a different story: since 1986, lows have risen +0.98°F per decade (95% range +0.70 to +1.26) and highs have risen +0.62°F per decade (95% range +0.22 to +1.02). The full record joins different observing sites over the years, and a move (for example, from the city to a cooler airport) can hide or exaggerate a long-run trend, so the recent decades are the clearer guide here.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in 2 of 12 months; January and April fell. Highs rose in 11 of 12 months.
text.t_rain: Rain and snow: no clear long-term change
text.p_rain: Chattanooga's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (+0.26 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 55.0 inches a year. The wettest year was 1994 (73.70 in); the driest, 1904 (32.68 in).
